events.text:
😲 America’s ‘unsinkable aircraft carrier’ just got wiped out by Iran
At its height, Naval Support Activity Bahrain (NSA Bahrain) housed ~8.5k troops, supported 30+ forward-deployed warships, and served as the primary operational hub and HQ of the US Fifth Fleet.
Wide-area maritime surveillance, regional early warning and point defense were made possible using an AR-327 long-range surveillance radar, a powerful AN/TPS-59 missile defense radar, and an AN/MPQ-65 fire-control radar. Integrated defenses included PAC-3 batteries and C-RAMs.
👉 Base C&C systems for C4I included Naval Computer & Telecommunications Station Bahrain – which tapped into EHF and AEHF satellite networks for real-time coordination and targeting. Paired with the Isa and Al Udeid air bases, NSA Bahrain packed firepower equivalent to that of whole nations.
Then, in the space of a just a few days, from late February-early March, the facility was pounded so hard by Iran that it was left a “virtually uninhabitable” hollowed-out husk. Retired US Navy Captain John Cordle characterizes the base’s fate as “unimaginable.”
💬 “The installation provides the physical infrastructure that keeps American military power continuously available in a strategically vital region. It is foundational to America’s ability to project maritime power in this critical theater,” Cordle lamented in a wistful MilitaryTimes op-ed.
Accordingly, “the idea that the US could not prevent and defend against a predictable attack on a Fleet Headquarters – and our sailors stationed there – is quite startling.”
Without access to the base, US Navy logistics and resupply have evacuated to Diego Garcia – some 2.2k+ nautical miles away. The Fifth Fleet’s HQ has fled to Florida.
💬 “The potential loss of NSA Bahrain is effectively the equivalent of losing an aircraft carrier,” Cordle complained. “If NSA Bahrain is not reconstituted to something near its pre-attack capabilities, it will fundamentally change how the US Navy operates, supplies and maintains its ships. It will also upend how we support regional coalition partners in the Gulf region.”
